newsitem.title: CANADA: Ontario economy could derail deficit plan - DBRS.
newsitem.headline: Ontario economy could derail deficit plan - DBRS.

text.p: Ontario's deficit reduction plan could be derailed if the economy of Canada's most-populous province weakened significantly over the next four years, a Canadian debt rating agency said on Tuesday.
The Conservative government has already cut about C$6 billion in public spending to elminate a projected 1995-96 deficit of C$8.7 billion by fiscal 2000-01.
The government is expected to unveil more cuts in a mini-budget next month, but Dominion Bond Rating Service Ltd warned it may not be enough to stay on target.
"An economic downturn anytime before the projected balanced budget date in 2000-01 is a significant risk to the government's plan," DBRS said in its fiscal outlook.

If Ontario's gross domestic product growth is one percentage point below forecast each year through 2000-01, an extra C$2.8 billion of program spending would have to be cut, according to the rating agency's estimates.

The government's 30 percent personal income tax is a major challenge to a balanced budget. About 88 percent of higher tax revenues from economic growth over the next three years will be needed to finance the tax rate reduction, DBRS said.

Declining transfer payments present another challenge to Ontario's balanced budget plan. DBRS estimated that federal transfers to Ontario will decline by C$2.4 billion, or 31.5 percent, by fiscal 1998-99.

"DBRS expects that the 1996-97 and 1997-98 deficit targets are achievable based on current fiscal action. Additional fiscal action will likely be required to meet the deficit targets in the later years of the plan," the rating agency said.
